extracted.intended_audience: individual humanities researchers and scholars applying for NEH Summer Stipends
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) Summer Stipends program, including required attachments, eligibility confirmations, and addressing peer-review criteria. This covers narrative construction, document formatting, letter-of-reference procedures, and compliance with program restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 1: Intellectual significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual significance of the proposed project, including its value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and describe the project's thesis or claim, overview of ideas/questions, and explain how the project complements, challenges, or expands relevant studies. The bibliography will be used to assess knowledge of the subject area. (See 'Significance and contribution' narrative guidance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 2: Quality of conception, organization, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address project organization and clarity in the narrative; include chapter outline for book projects, description of technologies for digital projects, annotations for editions/translations, and samples where applicable. Narrative sections align with this criterion, especially methodology/work plan and appendices for certain project types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 3: Feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed work plan and time line based on a full-time two-consecutive-month commitment. Do not depend heavily on factors beyond the applicant’s control (e.g., outside readers' reports). Explain steps to complete the project if not finished within the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 4: Quality or promise of quality of the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality or promise of quality of the applicant as an interpreter of the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate competence, relevant experience, language/digital skills, access to archives/collections, and past accomplishments. Include a two-page résumé with positions, education, awards, publications, and prior NEH support; résumé evaluated primarily under this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 5: Likelihood of completion and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the applicant will complete the project (not necessarily during the period of performance), including, when relevant, the soundness of the dissemination and access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intended audience, intended results, dissemination methods, publisher interest if any, language-of-publication implications, public access (free access preferred), and maintenance of digital outputs beyond the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative length and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative must be limited to three single-spaced pages with one-inch margins and a font size no smaller than eleven points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images, charts, diagrams, footnotes, and endnotes are allowed if they fit within the three-page limit. Use the required section headings and ensure clarity for non-specialist peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required narrative sections (crosswalk to review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative must include sections addressing significance and contribution; methodology and work plan; competencies, skills, and access; and final product and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH aligns these sections with review criteria (significance → criteria 1 & 2; methodology → 2 & 3; competencies → 2,3,4; dissemination → 5). For book projects include chapter outline; for digital projects describe technologies and public access; for translations provide rationale if other English translations exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography must not exceed a single page, with one-inch margins and font no smaller than eleven points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include primary and secondary sources that relate directly to the project’s substance and methods; evaluators use the bibliography primarily under review criterion 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Résumé requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Résumés must not exceed two pages and must be a résumé (not a narrative biographical statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current and past positions, education (degrees, dates, thesis/dissertation titles), awards/honors (with dates), publications/presentations (full citations), other professional activities, and language competence. Résumé evaluated primarily under review criterion 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices policy and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices are optional, limited to two pages, and are accepted only for specified project types (editions/translations, database projects, visual materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For editions/translations include one page original sample and one page edited/translated sample. Database projects: provide a one-page sample entry. Visual materials: provide a one-page sample converted to PDF. Any other appendices will not be reviewed. Appendices evaluated primarily under review criterion 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree conferral attachment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have satisfied all requirements for a degree but are awaiting conferral must include a letter from the dean or department chair attesting the applicant's status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the file degreeconferral.pdf and include as Attachment 5; this is conditionally required to establish eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of delinquent federal debt attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants delinquent in repayment of federal debt must provide explanatory information and evidence of repayment arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the file delinquentdebt.pdf and include as Attachment 6; where relevant, this may be used to assess eligibility and compliance with 2 CFR requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should solicit two letters of reference; provide names, e-mail addresses, and affiliations on the NEH supplemental form; letters are submitted online by NEH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters are more persuasive if they address the specific proposed activity and candidate's ability. For translations, one letter must be from a language expert addressing the sample translation. Letters must be submitted by specified deadlines; late letters may be added but reviewers might not consider them. Missing letters will not disqualify an application but may weaken it. Elected officials and current NEH Council members may not serve as letter writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — completion of formal education
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must have completed their formal education by the application deadline; applicants enrolled in degree-granting programs are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who have satisfied degree requirements but await conferral may apply if they include Attachment 5 (degree conferral letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — citizenship and residency
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens (resident inside or outside U.S.) are eligible; foreign nationals are eligible if they have lived in the United States or its jurisdictions for at least the three years immediately preceding the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate citizenship status on the SF-424. Applicants must provide accurate mailing and email addresses for notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty nomination requirement and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty holding tenured or tenure-track full-time positions at institutions of higher education must be nominated by their institutions; each institution may nominate two faculty members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must designate a single nominating official (usually an academic VP or dean) to run a fair competition and confirm nominees online after the application deadline. Exceptions (may apply without nomination): independent scholars, non-tenure-track faculty, community college faculty, emeritus faculty, and staff not teaching during the academic year preceding the award. Applicants whose nomination status is not confirmed will be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on applications and active NEH awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit only one application to the Summer Stipends program per year and are limited to having only one active NEH individual award at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant accepts another NEH individual award in the same fiscal year, the Summer Stipend application will be automatically withdrawn. Applicants may apply concurrently to certain other NEH competitions but may not hold overlapping NEH individual awards or participate in institutional awards that conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance — full-time two consecutive months
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Stipends support continuous full-time work on a humanities project for a period of two consecutive months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must work full-time on their projects for the awarded two months and may not accept teaching assignments or other activities that divert them during that time. Periods normally in summer but can be arranged for other times; indicate start/end dates on application. Provide a timeline in the narrative reflecting full-time commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Stipends provide $6,000 for two consecutive months of research and writing. NEH funds may support recipients’ compensation, travel, and other costs related to the proposed scholarly research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may receive travel and research-related expenses as part of the stipend. Recipients may hold other non-NEH sources of support during the stipend period, but may not hold another NEH individual award simultaneously. If stipend is paid through an institution, all NEH funds must be remitted to the individual (no institutional allowance permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable activities and funding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used for the development of teaching methods or theories; research by students enrolled in a degree program (including dissertations); training or coursework for the applicant; support for graduate student assistants; preparation or revision of textbooks; curriculum development; educational or technical impact assessments; promotion/advocacy of particular political/religious/ideological views; support of specific public policies or legislation; lobbying; projects outside the humanities (creation/performance of art; creative writing, autobiographies, memoirs, creative nonfiction; quantitative/policy-driven social science research); inventories of collections; writing of guide/how-to/self-help books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to individuals; indirect costs are unallowable. NEH does not make awards to other federal entities or to projects so closely intertwined with federal entities that they take on federal characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application package, submission mechanism, and Grants.gov requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must apply online through Grants.gov Workspace using the SF-424 - Individual package associated with the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Grants.gov registration in advance (NEH will not grant deadline extensions for lack of registration). Ensure workspace attachments are PDFs, named and ordered per the Application Components Table, and validated under the correct funding opportunity number before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment format, file naming, and PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments must be in Portable Document Format (.pdf). Limit file names to 50 or fewer characters; do not attach documents with the same name; use only specified UTF-8 characters when naming attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merge multiple documents into a single PDF for an attachment; do not attach zip files; improper file formats or naming may cause application rejection or processing issues. If Grants.gov validates an incomplete submission, NEH may still reject it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Title and Project Description field constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Title may not exceed 125 characters; Project Description must describe the project for a nonspecialist audience and must not exceed 1,000 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles should be descriptive, informative to a general audience, and avoid specialized language; NEH reserves the right to change titles for awarded projects. Exceeding character limits may lead to truncation or rejection by Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-U-N-S® (DUNS) requirement for affiliated applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with an institutional affiliation must include their institution’s D-U-N-S® number (omit hyphens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures NEH correctly identifies the institution in materials provided to external reviewers; typically provided by the institution’s sponsored research office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access preference and digital maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH gives preference to award products that provide free access to the public and expects digital materials produced with NEH funds to be maintained to ensure long-term availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain dissemination/access plans and any plans for paywalls or charges; describe how digital results will be maintained and supported beyond the project period. NEH retains a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce or use award products for federal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review, staff review, and final selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH staff review applications for eligibility and completeness; eligible applications are evaluated by peer reviewers and NEH staff provide comments before making recommendations to the National Council on the Humanities; the NEH Chairman makes final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers are experts instructed to evaluate according to the stated review criteria and must comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules. Award decisions are discretionary and not subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of risk and pre-award activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that receive favorable reviews are further assessed for past performance, eligibility, and compliance with public policy requirements before award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH may request additional information or require certain activities prior to award. Such requests do not guarantee an award; approving officials determine award eligibility, conditions, and funding level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit a final performance report within 90 calendar days after the period of performance ends; a final financial report is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final report collects information on accomplishments, products arising or anticipated, other financial support, project impact, and acknowledgement of NEH support. Reports submitted online through eGMS Reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate submissions and validation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is submitted more than once prior to the application due date, NEH will accept the last validated online submission under the correct funding opportunity number as the final and only acceptable application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct funding opportunity number and final validated submission are in place prior to the deadline. NEH may detect technical problems after retrieval and notify the applicant by email if an email address was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to register early and no deadline extensions for registration issues
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH strongly recommends completing Grants.gov registration at least two weeks before the application deadline; NEH will not grant deadline extensions for lack of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants fail to allow sufficient time for registration, they will not be given a deadline extension or waiver of the online submission requirement. Contact Grants.gov or NEH staff well ahead of the deadline for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget not required
rubrics_metrics.description: A budget is not required in this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although no budget attachment is required, applicants should still describe the use of NEH funds where relevant in the narrative and follow guidance about allowable costs.
